transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-07-07 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Nguyen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Michael Chen (Redwood CSM), Dr. Lena Ortiz (Bluepeak), Marcus Hale (Bluepeak), Sophie Park (Bluepeak Sec), Jon Reyes (Bluepeak DevOps)

Summary: Kickoff for onboarding Bluepeak Health onto Redwood. Confirmed use cases (clinical summarization + search), data residency and SOC2 requirements, preference for VPC/private deployment for PHI, initial pilot scope and timeline.

[00:00] Alex Nguyen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, I'll run the kickoff, with Priya our solutions engineer and Michael is the CSM. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Hi Lena here.
[00:15] Marcus Hale: Marcus, VP Eng.
[00:18] Sophie Park: Sophie, security lead.
[00:21] Jon Reyes: Jon, DevOps.
[00:25] Alex Nguyen: Awesome. Hi all. The goal for today is to align on architecture, compliance needs, initial pilot success criteria and next steps. We'll go over onboarding tasks, who does what, and timelines.

[02:05] Priya Rao: I'll give a short tech overview of Redwood and then dive into recommended setup for clinical workloads. Quick note - I might say Redifwood a couple times, sorry for the auto-transcript weirdness.
[02:20] Marcus Hale: Ha, no worries.

[03:00] Priya Rao: Redwood provides hosted API and a Dedicated/Private option. For PHI we usually recommend Private (VPC or on-prem), because you need customer-managed networking, KMS, audit logs. But we also support hosted if you can accept data-in-transit encryption and our SOC2 routine. For the pilot, what's your preference?
[03:22] Dr. Lena Ortiz: We need to handle PHI, so leaning private. Our infra can't have uncontrolled egress. We have AWS VPCs in us-east-1.
[03:38] Alex Nguyen: Got it. Private VPC peering is straightforward. We'll need your VPC CIDRs and a peering or transit gateway pattern. Jon, is that feasible?
[03:46] Jon Reyes: Yes we can do VPC peering. Need to review security groups and egress rules but doable.

[05:10] Sophie Park: From security perspective, SOC2 scope is mandatory. We have to validate encryption-at-rest keys and HSM/KMS practices. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
[05:20] Priya Rao: Yes, for Private deployments we support customer KMS integrations; on hosted we provide envelope encryption but not customer KMS by default. We can plug in your AWS KMS for key wrapping on the private control plane.
[05:35] Sophie Park: Ok good. Also need RBAC and audit logs for API calls - who called what model, token counts, etc.
[05:45] Michael Chen: Our Console has token-level logs and per-route dashboards; for Private we push audit logs to your CloudWatch/S3 or syslog. We'll share the logging schema.

[07:15] Marcus Hale: Let's talk performance. We expect low-latency inference for short clinical summarization tasks, average 250 tokens per call; target p95 under 700ms. Can Redwood meet that on private deployment?
[07:30] Priya Rao: Typical p95 depends on model and instance profile. For small-medium LLMs (7B-13B) with quantization and batching tuned we often see 300-600ms p95 for 250-token sequences on dedicated GPU pools. We'll recommend instance types and batching settings in the perf doc. For strict p95 <700ms we can propose reserved Dedicated or higher-tier hardware.
[08:05] Dr. Lena Ortiz: We want to balance cost and latency. For the pilot we'd accept slightly higher tail latency if cost savings are meaningful.
[08:12] Priya Rao: Makes sense - we'll provide a couple of profiles: one latency-optimized (higher cost) and one cost-optimized (lower cost, some tail).

[09:00] Alex Nguyen: On the business side, Michael will manage entitlements and quotas. For the pilot what's the expected throughput?
[09:10] Marcus Hale: Initially a few hundred requests per day, spiking to maybe 5k/day during testing.
[09:18] Michael Chen: That fits a small Dedicated pool or even Private with burst capacity. We'll propose auto-scale thresholds.

[11:00] Jon Reyes: Network/topology questions - do you require inbound peering only or do you initiate connections from your side?
[11:10] Priya Rao: For private deployments we can do VPC peering or PrivateLink. Typically the customer's infra peers to Redwood's serving VPC; no public egress required. We'll send a network checklist.

[13:20] Sophie Park: Audit and compliance: do you have SOC2 Type II report and can we run an audit?
[13:30] Michael Chen: Redwood is SOC2 compliant; we provide the report under NDA and have a compliance packet. For Private we provide additional artifacts around logging and configuration.

[15:00] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Data residency - all data must remain in us-east-1. Any cross-region fallback?
[15:10] Priya Rao: We'll pin your deployment to us-east-1; automated fallback to other regions only if you opt-in. For pilot we'll keep it in-region.

[17:40] Marcus Hale: Integration questions - we want to call Redwood from our backend APIs. SDKs? REST?
[17:50] Alex Nguyen: We have REST and SDKs (Python, Node). For private you'll get a private endpoint and service account keys. We'll walk through key rotation and RBAC.

[20:05] Dr. Lena Ortiz: For the pilot, sample data will be de-identified. After we prove the pipeline we'll bring in PHI and need the Private arrangement.
[20:20] Michael Chen: Sounds good. We'll stage it: PoC with de-id data on hosted or private dev cluster, then full PHI on private-prod.

[22:10] Priya Rao: Operational notes: caching and batching will affect latency and cost. For clinical summarization, prefix KV caching can reduce tokens for follow-up requests. We'll propose caching TTLs.
[22:30] Jon Reyes: Will caching be under our control? We want to be able to invalidate keys programmatically.
[22:36] Priya Rao: Yes, you can control cache invalidation via the Console/SDK.

[25:00] Sophie Park: About model selection - any recommendations for hallucination rate vs latency?
[25:10] Priya Rao: Tradeoff depends on model size and finetune. For high-fidelity clinical summarization we suggest a vetted 13B that we've verified; if hallucination is critical we can run reranker or run eval sets. We'll share eval results from similar customers.
[25:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Great - we want to see the evals.

[28:00] Alex Nguyen: Next, timeline. For onboarding we propose: week 1 gather network and SSO details, week 2 infra setup and RBAC, week 3 pilot perf tests, week 4 user validation. Does that map to your expectations?
[28:18] Marcus Hale: Yes that's reasonable. We want the pilot to start in two weeks.

[30:00] Michael Chen: I'll kick off with a calendar invite for regular check-ins. Also sending the onboarding checklist.

[31:40] Sophie Park: SSO details - we use Okta and SAML 2.0. We'll send metadata. We also need IP allowlist and SCIM for provisioning.
[31:55] Priya Rao: Okta + SAML + SCIM supported. We'll send the SAML entity and ACS URLs for the private control plane.

[34:10] Jon Reyes: For deployment we'll likely use a Transit Gateway. We'll export VPC flow logs and look for allowed ports.
[34:20] Priya Rao: We'll share minimal port list and healthcheck endpoints.

[37:00] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Who will own the pilot success metrics?
[37:05] Alex Nguyen: We suggest jointly owned: Redwood provides latency and token metrics; Bluepeak provides accuracy and business metrics (reduction in manual review time, user acceptance).
[37:18] Dr. Lena Ortiz: We'll define success as p95 < 700ms and F1 for extraction task above 0.88 on our eval set.

[39:40] Marcus Hale: Budget - can you provide estimated cost for a 30-day pilot (private infra plus support)?
[39:50] Michael Chen: We'll send a cost estimate and a couple of sizing options.

[42:10] Sophie Park: Legal/procurement - we need a DPA and BAA for PHI.
[42:20] Alex Nguyen: We have standard DPA and can provide BAA for private deployments; legal will follow up. We'll attach legal contacts.

[44:30] Priya Rao: On testing, we'd like to run a small benchmark. If you can provide a sample de-id dataset we can run a perf and quality run and share results.
[44:45] Dr. Lena Ortiz: We'll send a 200-record sample by end of week.

[47:00] Jon Reyes: For logging, do you push logs to our S3 or CloudWatch?
[47:05] Michael Chen: We can push to either. We'll provide the schema and retention options.

[49:20] Alex Nguyen: Recap of next steps: we'll send onboarding deck, network checklist, SSO metadata endpoints, perf/cost profiles, and SOC2 artifacts under NDA. Bluepeak to send network diagram, Okta metadata, and sample dataset.

[50:10] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. One more question - does Redwood have reference architecture for disaster recovery?
[50:20] Priya Rao: Yes, for private we have DR patterns (multi-AZ within region, warm standby in another region if required). We'll include DR notes.

[52:00] Marcus Hale: OK thanks everyone. 
[52:05] Alex Nguyen: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the docs and invites.
[52:12] Michael Chen: I'll send the first follow-up email with attachments.
[52:25] Sophie Park: Thanks.
[52:30] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Thanks.

Meeting ended ~16:55 PDT.

References shared: onboarding deck (link withheld), network checklist (link withheld), SOC2 report (under NDA), perf spreadsheet (link withheld).

Action items (restated): Alex to send onboarding deck and calendar invites; Priya to share perf and model recommendations; Michael to provide compliance pack; Bluepeak to share network diagram, Okta SAML metadata, and sample dataset.
